name: Slack Desk
description: Builds memory from your Slack conversations and surfaces anything that looks like a task you missed. Reads only — it never posts.
_comment: Runs OUT OF PROCESS, spawned by app-process.ts: own port, own store, reachable only over the lifecycle and data seams. Built entirely on @flock/app-sdk, which the PLATFORM supplies into node_modules at build time — its correct version is whatever this Flock build speaks, so it is not resolved from a registry. THE APP IS THE INSTALLABLE UNIT: no owning skill, because `config.requires` below declares the connector it needs and `routines` declares the work it does, and pairing grants both to the agent.

agent.label: Agent that reads your Slack and remembers what matters

routines.name: Build memory from Slack
routines.description: Once a day, reads the channels you chose and remembers what matters — plus anything that reads like a task you have not done. No AI cost beyond the daily extraction; nothing is ever posted.
routines._cronComment: HOURLY DISPATCH, DAILY WORK (2026-09-25). The work is still once a day — harvestRanToday gates it — but a pass that stops on its read or block budget leaves the day UNCLAIMED so a later tick finishes it. At 0 5 * * * there was no later tick: a capped first landing waited until tomorrow. Email Desk resolved the same tension the same way. :17 rather than :00 to sit off the hour with everything else.
routines._triggerComment: schedule + app-relay (executor: cron.ts dispatchScheduledAppRelays). NOT event + app-relay: this app fetches its own Slack data through /apps/:id/skill-exec, so a platform connector poll on its behalf would be a second read of the same messages.

configSchema.label: How far back to read each day (hours)
Only remember conversations that involve you
configSchema.help: Off: read everything in the channels above and log what would have been skipped. On: skip conversations in channels you did not pick where you are neither mentioned nor speaking.
configSchema._comment: OFF IS THE DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. Off computes the same verdict and ignores it, so a week of logs says what turning it on WOULD have cost in memory before anyone risks it. A channel picked above always keeps full extraction either way — a pick is the owner saying watch this.

configSchema.label: Most conversations to extract in one pass
configSchema._comment: A ceiling on a day's spend. A pass that hits it defers the rest, records why it stopped, and leaves the day claimable so the next hourly tick resumes it — ranked so what concerns the owner goes first and a deferred conversation ages into priority.
